`Webflow doesn't sell a one-time product` ; instead, you sign up for **Workspace Plans** (for building/collaborating) and **Site Plans** (for hosting and launching a live website).[[1]](https://webflow.com/pricing)

You can pick and purchase your subscription directly on the [Webflow Pricing Page](https://webflow.com/pricing).

### **1. Site Plans (Hosting & Publishing)** 

- **Starter:** Free ($0/mo) — Great for testing out the builder or personal experiments (with a `.webflow.io` domain).
- **Basic:** $15/mo *(billed yearly)* — Best for simple sites, landing pages, and portfolios (supports a custom domain and up to 300 static pages).
- **Premium:** $25/mo *(billed yearly)* — Combines CMS and business features for content-rich sites, blogs, and higher traffic.
- **Ecommerce Plans:** Standard ($29/mo), Plus ($74/mo), and Advanced ($212/mo) — For online stores managing product catalogs and checkouts.[[1]](https://help.webflow.com/hc/en-us/articles/51059955082387-Updated-pricing-and-simplified-plans-for-May-2026)[[2]](https://webflow.com/pricing)

### **2. Workspace Plans (Designers & Teams)** 

- **Starter:** Free ($0/mo) — For individual freelancers starting out (1 seat, limited staging sites).
- **Core:** $19/mo *(billed yearly)* — For freelancers and small designers needing custom code export and more staging slots.
- **Growth:** $49/mo *(billed yearly)* — For growing teams and agencies with unlimited staging sites and added collaboration features.[[1]](https://webflow.com/pricing)

### **How to Get Started** 

1. Create a free account on the Webflow Signup Page.
2. Build and design your site in the visual canvas.
3. Upgrade your specific project or workspace to a paid plan inside your project settings when you're ready to connect a custom domain.

Are you building a **standard portfolio/landing page** , a **blog/content site** , or an **e-commerce store** ? Let me know so I can recommend the exact plan combination you need.
